result:
The final answer of 50 is not supported, so I reject it.

The proposed solution never identifies a specific graph with 50 vertices. It names a "Möbius strip graph" and asserts it has 50 vertices "in some specific embeddings," with no construction or citation. The Möbius strip is not a standard planar 4-regular graph, so the claim is also internally inconsistent with the hypothesis that G is planar. The solution then says the theorem "fails" for this graph without checking any conflict-free cut condition.

A small candidate is the octahedron, a simple connected planar 4-regular graph on 6 vertices. Its minimal cuts are the vertex stars (size 4), the edge-induced bonds (size 6), and the triangle-face bonds (size 6). For a perfect-matching conflict graph, one can try to force every such cut to contain a matched pair. Pairing the two in-edges at each vertex of an Eulerian orientation kills all six stars, but I did not finish checking the size-6 cuts. So I am not certain the octahedron is the answer. Either way, nothing in the proposed solution supports 50.

VERDICT: REJECT
CONFIDENCE: 4
